topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the scope of the course, its target audience, and the key learning outcomes for cancer biology.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer at the cellular and tissue levels as a breakdown of differentiation and structural organization driven by genetic changes, alongside the experimental models used to investigate them.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and benign-to-malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the clinical, histological, and biological distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on mechanisms of tissue invasion, metastatic dissemination, and stepwise progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and notable exceptions used to name benign and malignant tumors according to their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the mechanical, systemic, and metastatic processes through which tumors disrupt normal physiological function to cause disease and death.

topics.label: Comparative tumor incidence and cancer across multicellular organisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor prevalence across human tissue types and diverse animal species to frame cancer as an inherent risk of multicellular development.

topics.label: Clinical cancer screening principles and tissue modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, histological basis, and practical efficacy of clinical screening programs across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a summary of learning outcomes and logistical reminders for upcoming practicals.
